task_description: Bound the two chunker shapes that escaped the token budget (markdown fence-swallowing, code single-line-over-budget), both MEASURED during the first real vault ingest
test_results: MEASURED after the fix (quoted from commit message): the one-line JSON shape goes from 1 chunk to 27, max 200 tokens / 680 chars. The fenced-note shape no longer merges prose into the block. Exact-offset invariant (chunk.text == text[char_start:char_end], gaps whitespace-only) asserted for every new shape.
errors: markdown.py: a fence-open transition appended to the buffer without flushing it, so prose sitting just under max_tokens absorbed an entire fenced block before any size check could fire. A real note produced a single 28,446-character (~8,366-token) chunk against a 200-token target.

code.py: the line window could never shrink below one whole physical line, so a one-line 12,623-character .json file became a single chunk, which the embedding service rejects with `422 texts[0] exceeds 8000 characters`.

Regression fixtures are synthetic -- the vault is a read-only source root and never a fixture source; both defects were MEASURED during the real vault ingest in 37b90da, then fixed here with synthetic reproductions.

Remaining limitation, by design (module rule 1): a *standalone* fence larger than the budget is still one oversized chunk -- measured at 10,191 chars, still above the embedder's 8,000-char limit, so the pipeline's hard-split backstop and MiniLM's 256-token truncation still apply to those. Whether rule 1 should yield to the embedding limit is an open design question for A07b/A02, not resolved here.
architecture_decisions: Fence open and close are now hard boundaries like an ATX heading: unconditional, deliberately not size-gated, because a size gate at the fence boundary is no gate at all -- prose under the budget passes it and the block lands on top regardless.

A single line over budget is now split within the line -- the one place this chunker cuts inside a line, because no smaller natural unit exists; prefers the last whitespace inside the budget, cuts mid-token only when there is none (the minified-JSON case).
Both module rules still hold and are covered by tests: a fenced block is never split, and a `#` inside a fence is never a heading.
handoffs: A02 -- open design question on whether chunking rule 1 should yield to the 8,000-char embedding limit for standalone oversized fences
